problems_found: MISLABELLED/MIXED MACHINE-READABLE FIELD, section 3: the JSON key loglog_fit_vmax_ge_0.1 carries n = 16 (the vmax>=0.1 subset count) but its slope = 0.009894, A = 0.058752, R2 = 0.003257 and max_residual_dex = 0.451186 are the ALL-19 fit. Recomputing: ALL 19 levels -> slope +0.009894, R2 0.003257, maxres 0.451186; vmax>=0.1 (n=16) -> slope -0.082530, R2 0.204143, maxres 0.324301. The field therefore mixes a subset count with an all-levels fit. The section-3 verdict and section-7 conclusion ('slope -0.082, R2 0.204') match the vmax>=0.1 fit and are numerically correct; the -0.082/0.204 also appear in the earlier explore output _t3e8.txt. So the load-bearing prose is right, but any downstream consumer reading the JSON field keyed vmax_ge_0.1 gets the wrong fit's coefficients (abs diff 0.092 in slope, 0.201 in R2 vs the cut it names).

INTERNAL CONTRADICTION, section 6: the stored two_sinusoid_separation_test_pass01 field gives fraction_of_trials_resolved_two_peaks = 0.75 at 250 uHz and 0.88 at 275 uHz, but the section-6 'verdict' and section-7 conclusion state '55% of trials at 250 uHz but 95-100% at 275-325 uHz'. 0.55/0.95 are stale values from _t3_explore10.py (printed to _t3e10.txt lines 19-20) obtained with only 20 trials; the current script uses 200 trials and yields 0.75/0.88. Both 275 (0.88) and 250 (0.75) are misreported.

FORMATTING DEFECT: 3 literal '%%' tokens survive in the stored JSON strings (section 1 conclusion '11.2%%', section 6 verdict '55%%' and '95-100%%', section 7 conclusion 0). The %%-escaped strings were never passed through a % formatter, so the result file shipped with unrendered percent signs. Cosmetic for the arithmetic, but it confirms the prose was written by hand rather than generated from the printed values.

HARD-CODED RESULT VALUES, section 2: single_grid_step_cost_at_optimum (14.1/12.8/25.3/10.1/20.6/1.1) and the whole interior_curvature_at_vmax30 block are literals in the script, not computed there. I recomputed them independently from candidate_spectrum_comparison.tsv and they are exactly right (max |diff| 7e-15), so this is a traceability defect, not a numerical error.

INCONSISTENT TERMINOLOGY, section 3: the section-3 verdict calls -0.082/0.204 the fit for 'the flat, non-monotonic valley' while the JSON field that holds these numbers is truncated at vmax >= 0.1. Recomputing all natural variant cuts (all-19, >=0.1, >=1, >=5, interior-only), the value -0.082530 / R2 0.204143 appears only for the vmax >= 0.1 cut; the full 19-level star gives +0.009894 / 0.003257 and the vmax >= 5 cut gives +0.1806 / 0.3713, so the quoted slope is cut-dependent and not a single robust description of the valley.

OVERSTATED CLAIM, section 3: 'residual scatter corresponds to +-1 grid step'. Recomputed on the fa ridge (f_star = 709.29 * vmax^0.121366), residuals are max 73.64 uHz / rms 43.17 uHz, i.e. max 1.47 x the 50 uHz grid step and rms 0.86 x. The '+-1 step' figure is at best an rms statement and is false as a bound.
MIS-STATEMENT, section 4: 'Adding interactions nearly doubles R2 (0.024 -> 0.138)'. 0.0236 -> 0.1382 is a 5.9x increase, not a doubling.

MINOR LOGIC OVERREACH, section 1: the 'FN = 1' cell (minimum_velocity_scan, vmax=20, vmin=0.02, f=1210, w=300, ic = 137.2) is actually present in the ranked table at candidate_rank 250 with ic = 137.2. It is counted as a false negative only because the stated admission rule is the strict inequality 'ic < 137.2' while the table is a top-250 cut whose last cell ties the cutoff. The truncation conclusion is unaffected (28/28 cells with ic < 137.2 present, 0 false positives), but the ledger as printed is off by this boundary tie.

TRUNCATION COVERAGE IS WORSE THAN THE HEADLINE: the table covers 250/2240 = 11.2%, but the candidate file independently evidences only 105 distinct lattice cells and the union of the two files evidences 326/2240 = 14.6%. 1914 of the 2240 declared cells (85.4%) never appear in ANY supplied file, so the 'remaining 1990 cells' framing understates the unobserved region: 1914 cells could not be checked even in principle. The track's own conclusion already says the 88.4% is censored, so this sharpens rather than reverses it.
checks_that_found_nothing: (a) No treatment of adjacent time samples or grid rows as independent replicates was found: pass-level statistics use n=22 whole passes and grid quantities are marginal minima/margins over cells, not reported as replicated measurements.

(b) No p-value or CI is blocked at the wrong level: the only p-values quoted are the mode-alignment permutation-style nulls, whose draws are independent uniform frequencies (a legitimate chance null), not time samples or grid rows. The section-2 separation is correctly reported as a margin ladder, with the absence of replicate IC on delta-IC explicitly stated.

(c) The track does NOT claim the ranked grid is a complete cartesian grid; it explicitly calls it a top-250 truncation of a 2240-cell lattice and states the rank-1 cell is only best among the 250 survivors.

(d) No physical-uniqueness claim is made from the relative IC comparison; the relative-only caveat list explicitly says the IC comparisons are conditional on the supplied families and that marginal 'best axis level' values are not physical optima.

(f) The mode-alignment claim is tested against three chance nulls (uniform over the mode range, uniform over the candidate band, rigid 50 uHz comb with free phase) with 100k-200k draws each; my own-seed reruns reproduce every null median and p to Monte-Carlo precision.

(g) No null result was traced to a bug: the 'not closer than chance' conclusion is corroborated by the in-band mode spacing (median 20.69 uHz) being 2.4x denser than the 50 uHz comb, which mechanically guarantees small nearest-mode offsets; the surrogates/draws are independent of the observed modes.
